function.description: Shuffles a deck of cards. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Step | What to Do | Why it matters | |------|------------|----------------| | 1. **Deal** | Shuffle a standard Uno deck (108 cards). Deal 7 cards to each player. Place the remaining cards face‑down to form the draw pile. Turn the top card over to start the discard pile. | Sets up the game and gives everyone a starting hand. | | 2. **Match or Play** | On your turn, you may play one card from your hand that matches the discard pile’s **color**, **number**, or **symbol** (Skip, Reverse, Draw Two, Wild, Wild Draw Four). | The core mechanic: you must match something to play. | | 3. **Wild Cards** | A Wild card can be played on any card. When you play it, you declare the new color. A Wild Draw Four can only be played if you have no other playable card (unless you’re bluffing). | Allows you to change the game’s direction or force opponents to draw. | | 4. **Special Actions** | • **Skip** – Next player loses a turn.
• **Reverse** – Reverses play order.
• **Draw Two** – Next player draws two cards and loses a turn.
• **Wild Draw Four** – Next player draws four cards and loses a turn. | Adds strategy and excitement. | | 5. **Draw** | If you can’t play a card, draw one from the draw pile. If that card is playable, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | Keeps the game moving even when you’re stuck. | | 6. **Uno** | When you have one card left, shout “UNO!” before your next opponent plays. If you forget and someone catches you, you must draw two cards as a penalty. | Signals you’re about to win; missing it costs you. | | 7. **Winning** | The first player to play all their cards wins the round. Score points based on the cards left in opponents’ hands (number cards = face value, Skip/Reverse/Draw Two = 20, Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50). | Determines the winner and keeps score. | **Quick Tips** - Keep a mix of colors and numbers to stay flexible. - Use Wild cards strategically to change the color when you’re stuck. - Pay attention to opponents’ cards; if they’re close to UNO, you might want to play a Skip or Draw Two to stop them. That’s it! Grab a deck, shuffle, and you’re ready to play Uno. Enjoy the fast‑paced fun and the occasional “UNO” shout‑out.
